deep.reconstruction:
Context: bundle R.ElektrCyl contains Riemann's draft on the equilibrium of electricity on parallel cylinders of circular cross-section. A fragment on this subject appears in his posthumous Werke, edited by Weber and Dedekind with Hattendorf's help. The page is a transition in a lecture or memoir draft, marked 'Riemann 5'.

(1) Transitional text. Having finished his remarks on convergence of integrals, Riemann turns to the integral of the partial differential equation that is the subject of the work.

(2) Statement of the problem. Find a function w(z) of the complex variable z = x + iy, defined on the region of the plane exterior to given circles (here three: C_0, C_1, C_2). Its real part u = Re w must take arbitrarily prescribed values on the circumferences. This is the Dirichlet problem for Laplace's equation in a domain bounded by three circles. Physically, u is the potential in a cross-section of three parallel charged cylinders.

(3) Figure. Three circles labelled p_0, p_1^(1), p_2^(2). Each has a marked boundary point with a small semicircular indentation. My interpretation: these are the points where the auxiliary function zeta has its poles, and the integration path is indented around them, as in the boundary integral on the next page (int d log ... = 0, with contributions -3 pi i and +3 pi i).

(4) Method: an auxiliary function zeta.
- z (written Z) is to be regarded as a function of zeta.
- zeta is purely real on the circumferences of the three circles.
- zeta is infinite for three values. My reading: one simple pole on each circle, at the marked points.
- zeta takes each real value only three times.

Completion (mine). zeta then maps each circle bijectively onto the extended real line. By the argument principle it maps the triply connected exterior region three-to-one onto a half-plane: for non-real w the winding number of zeta(boundary) about w counts the solutions. Hence the inverse z(zeta) is a three-valued function with branches z_1, z_2, z_3.

This is exactly what the next page exploits. Symmetric functions of the branches, such as z_1+z_2+z_3, are single-valued. The cubic (zeta' - zeta_1')(zeta' - zeta_2')(zeta' - zeta_3') = 0 has coefficients rational in zeta, of degree 3. The previous page notes that Z''/Z is an algebraic function of zeta. So the boundary-value problem is reduced to algebraic-function theory on a three-sheeted surface over the zeta-plane, the conformal analogue of Schwarz–Christoffel-type reductions for circular domains.
errors: No computational errors on this page; it is a problem statement plus an outline of method.

The existence of a function zeta, real on all three circles, with exactly three (boundary) poles and taking each real value exactly three times, is asserted without proof. It is true: a real-on-boundary function of this degree exists on the Schottky double, which has genus 2. But it requires justification, e.g. by Dirichlet's principle, which Riemann would invoke.

The phrase transcribed 'zeta - a jeden reellen Werth nur dreimal annehmen kann' is loose. What is meant is that zeta takes each real value a exactly three times, i.e. zeta - a has three zeros, one on each circle.

results.what: Formulation of the Dirichlet problem for the region exterior to three circles (potential of three parallel circular cylinders)
results.modern_name: Dirichlet problem in a multiply (triply) connected circular domain
results.usually_credited_to: Classical potential-theory problem; Riemann's electrostatics fragment (Werke, 1876); later Schottky (1877) and C. Neumann

results.what: Reduction via an auxiliary function zeta, real on all boundary circles, with three boundary poles, taking each real value three times, so that z(zeta) is three-valued and its symmetric functions are rational in zeta
results.modern_name: Real (Schottky-double) function of degree 3 / branched covering of a half-plane by a circular domain; Schottky-type uniformization of multiply connected domains
results.usually_credited_to: Schottky (1877 dissertation) for multiply connected circular domains; Riemann's posthumous fragment on cylinders already contains the idea

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to Riemann's known draft on electricity on parallel circular cylinders; a version is published in his Werke and recognized as anticipating Schottky's work on circular domains. The page adds only the problem statement and the qualitative properties of the auxiliary function zeta, which are consistent with the published fragment.

checkable.asserts: One-circle model: the Cayley-type function zeta = i(z+1)/(z-1) is real on |z|=1, with a single pole at the boundary point z=1. This is the one-circle analogue of zeta real on each circle with a boundary pole; the expected result is 0.
In the one-circle model each value w is taken exactly once (degree 1). With three circles the analogous degree is 3, giving the three branches z1, z2, z3.

checkable.sympy: zeta,s1,s2,s3,X=symbols('zeta s1 s2 s3 X'); expand((X-s1)*(X-s2)*(X-s3))
checkable.asserts: Coefficients of the cubic in zeta' are the elementary symmetric functions of the three branches. These are single-valued, hence rational in zeta, as used on the next page.

transcription_corrections: Line 6 'für alle Werthe der Ebene außerhalb ... die einfachsten Fälle gegebener Kreise' is more plausibly read as '... außerhalb ... dreier gegebener Kreise'. 'die einfachsten Fälle' is doubtful.
'Länge' at the start of line 8 is uncertain; it may belong to a phrase like '... gegebener Kreise Lage', i.e. circles of given position.
'z eine Function von zeta' appears in the image with a capital Z ('Z ein Function von zeta'), consistent with Z on the previous and next pages.

The figure labels read p_0, p_1^(1) (possibly p_1^(4)) and p_2^(2). Each circle carries a small semicircular indentation at a boundary point, probably marking the poles of zeta around which the path is indented.
'zeta - a jeden reellen Werth' may be 'zeta = a, jeden reellen Werth'; the meaning is that zeta takes each real value three times.
